subject: Re: POC Trial - Model selection & success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@acme-retail.com>; Daniel Cho <daniel@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: POC follow-up: success criteria & next steps

Hi Elena / Daniel —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap of the call and proposed next steps so we all have alignment: 

1) Primary goal for the POC (2 weeks): evaluate user-facing search+assistant experience for ACME product pages with multilingual support (EN/ES/FR) and ensure latency < 350ms p50 for the 99th percentile query pattern.

2) Success criteria (proposal):
- Quality: mean human eval score >= 4.0 on a 1-5 rubric across 150 sampled queries per language
- Performance: 350ms p50 and 800ms p95 on our dedicated test harness
- Cost: per-1M-token inference cost estimate within target budget provided during call

3) Evaluation plan: Redwood provides a test harness, seed prompt set (will use POC-Eval-Template.xlsx), and guidance for automated metrics + human annotation. ACME provides representative request logs (anonymized) and top 150 end-to-end user queries per language.

4) Model selection (initial recommendation): run two variants in parallel for 2 weeks:
- Primary: Llama-2-13B (int8 quantized) — best balance of quality & latency for generative search
- Fallback: Mistral-Instruct-7B (quantized) — lower-cost fallback for high-throughput queries and cold starts
We will also provision a multilingual-capable checkpoint for Spanish/French prompts and test cross-lingual retrieval.

5) Ownership & timeline:
- ACME: deliver anonymized logs + dataset by Feb 13
- Redwood (Marissa/Ben): provision infra, configs, and evaluation prompts by Feb 16
- Commencement of POC: Feb 18 — 2 weeks

6) Next steps:
- Elena: confirm data delivery timeline and any compliance constraints
- Daniel: share the list of power users for initial human eval
- Redwood: send SOW draft and POC evaluation template (attached)

Attachments: POC-Eval-Template.xlsx, SOW-Draft.docx

If that all looks right I’ll send a calendar invite for Feb 18 kickoff and lock in the infra.

Thanks,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks — adding technical detail for the POC model lineup and evaluation hooks so the infra team can provision correctly: 

Model variants:
- primary_variant: Llama-2-13B (int8) running on A100d instances with KV-cache enabled. Rationale: strong instruction-following and solid multilingual transfer when fine-tuned/prompted properly.
- fallback_variant: Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) using smaller GPU profile for burst handling. Rationale: faster cold starts, lower cost for high-throughput queries.
- safety/sanitization: add an output sanitization step for localized content and a simple profanity filter for user-facing responses.

Evaluation metrics & harness:
- auto_metrics: BLEU/ROUGE not great for open assistant — we’ll capture embedding-similarity + reward-model proxies plus generation length and token counts.
- human_eval: 150 queries per language, 6 SMEs, rating rubric: relevance, factuality, style match, helpfulness (1-5). We’ll provide a calibration doc and a shared Sheet for scoring.

Multilingual approach:
- prompts: language-tagging + exemplar prompts; detect language client-side where possible.
- retrieval: use ACME’s localized product descriptions as retrieval docs; run cross-lingual dense retrieval if needed.

Fallback policy:
- route queries that exceed latency SLO or have low confidence score to Mistral-Instruct-7B with a short prompt prefix indicating concise responses.

Infra & config checklist for Feb 16 provisioning:
- 2x Llama-2-13B nodes (A100d), int8 runtime, KV cache
- 3x Mistral-7B nodes for capacity and fallback
- logging hooks for latency, token counts, and model confidence

I attached the model quantization options doc and a draft SOW. Ben — can you confirm we have budget for the A100 nodes in the ACME POC quote?

Thanks,
Marissa
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
